audit.why: Favoured 4/10 matches 54.31% over 1125 games, and both layers already agree on the chart (Irelia all seven rows). Difficulty verdict left alone; the prose under it was templated and got grounded instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] and spikes[1] both call Comeuppance 'his revive ult'. The revive is Going Rogue (W), not R.
audit.why: enemyKit W text: killing a Scoundrel resurrects the allies they killed. enemyKit R text: locks onto a champion, stores bullets, damage based on missing health, stopped by the first champion, minion or structure hit. Two different abilities and the page merged them.
audit.corrected: Level 6 for Akshan is a 100/85/70 ranged missing-health nuke you body-block with a minion; the revive is a W mechanic that needs him to kill a Scoundrel.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags that the page names none of Akshan's abilities and gives zero sequencing cues. Three real interactions were absent: the Dirty Fighting shield, Heroic Swing's terrain requirement and collision knock-off, and Comeuppance being blocked by the first minion in its path.
audit.why: enemyKit P (shield every third hit from attacks AND abilities), E (hooks terrain; 'gets knocked off when colliding with champions or terrain'), R ('first champion, minion, or structure hit'). Also missingInteractions rule shield-absorbs-burst.
audit.corrected: Force the shield on the wave before committing; fight him in open lane where there is no wall to hook; keep a minion between you and a channelling Comeuppance.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (lint).
audit.corrected: Rewritten around those numbers plus what each one needs to work.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] says 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain'. Akshan has no heal — Dirty Fighting grants a shield.
audit.why: enemyKit P flag is 'shield', not 'heal'. Grievous Wounds does nothing to a shield.
audit.corrected: Replaced with a note to bait the shield rather than buy anti-heal.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] referred to Akshan kiting with 'auto-crit W'. W is Going Rogue — camouflage and the Scoundrel revive, not an attack modifier.
audit.why: enemyKit W text describes camouflage, Move Speed and Mana Regen while moving toward Scoundrels.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around Avengerang's 9s cooldown, which is the actual kiting tool.

edits.before: A duel of windows — his burst versus your sustain; stack before his commit and the stat check votes Ionian.
edits.after: Dirty Fighting shields him every third hit — force the shield out first, then commit with four stacks.

edits.before: Stat-check the assassin every window he doesn't one-shot you in. Shorthand: Heroic Swing down, wave right, go.
edits.after: Deny him range: Avengerang trades at 850, you trade at zero. Shorthand: Heroic Swing down, wave right, go.

edits.before: Akshan wins by landing Heroic Swing, denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.
edits.after: Akshan wins by kiting at 850 with Avengerang, shielding off every third hit, and swinging out before you land E.

edits.before: - Akshan Heroic Swing: matchup-defining — His swing engage/escape — fight only while it is down. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Defiant Dance like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Heroic Swing: 18s at rank 1, and he needs terrain to hook — colliding with a champion knocks him off it. - Avengerang: 9s at rank 1, 850 range. - Comeuppance: 100/85/70, stopped by the first minion in its path.

edits.before: W joins: the channel shreds incoming damage — hold it for his trade spell, not his autos.
edits.after: W joins: charge it as he winds up Avengerang at 850 — the 9s cooldown is your step-up window.

edits.before: Vanguard's Edge online — the all-in caps with a wall of disengage-proof marks. Dive with the wave as your fuel.
edits.after: Vanguard's Edge blocks the path he swings out along — cut the hook line and Heroic Swing has nowhere to go.

edits.before: Ahead, dance louder: crash waves into Akshan's face, stun the answers, and surf resets through every river fight.
edits.after: Ahead, take the walls off him: fight in open lane, and every Heroic Swing he burns is 18 seconds of free pressure.

edits.before: You are the front-to-back blender: Q through their line, stun the carries, and let the marks ground the peel.
edits.after: Comeuppance hits the first thing in its path — stand a minion or your own body between him and the carry.

edits.before: His swing engage/escape — fight only while it is down. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Heroic Swing is 18s at rank 1 and needs a wall to hook — fight him in open lane where he cannot swing out.

edits.before: W the burst, stun the exit
edits.after: Break his shield, then go

edits.before: Q-reset through two low minions onto his chest, four-stack autos, E-stun the retreat — the wave-funded all-in he budgeted zero for.
edits.after: Dirty Fighting shields him on every third hit from his attacks and abilities — eat that shield on the wave before you all-in.

edits.before: Akshan spends Heroic Swing early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Akshan spends Heroic Swing early — you have 18 seconds and he has no other exit.

edits.before: Your dashes live in the wave's health bar — shoving mindlessly is deleting your own mobility.
edits.after: Comeuppance scales on your missing health — at low HP his 2500-range ult finishes you from off-screen.

edits.before: Dashing in under-stacked with W down — Irelia without the engine is a melee minion with a famous haircut.
edits.after: Off the wave you have no dashes and Comeuppance reaches 2500 — the chase ends with his bullets in your back.

edits.before: Start Doran's Blade + pot. Blade of the Ruined King into Berserker's, then Wit's End/Steelcaps paths — on-hit is the language. Add anti-heal early into his sustain.
edits.after: Start Doran's Blade + pot. Blade of the Ruined King into Berserker's, then Wit's End/Steelcaps paths — on-hit is the language. He shields, not heals — bait it, skip anti-heal.

edits.before: Level 6: his revive ult is reactive, not proactive, so it rarely saves a lost fight.
edits.after: Level 6: Comeuppance is a 2500-range nuke, not the revive — the revive is Going Rogue (W).

edits.before: Q-E combo closes the gap before he can kite with auto-crit W.
edits.after: Q-E closes the gap before Avengerang's 9s cooldown comes back up.

edits.before: His revive ult only matters if he's already ahead; punish before it comes online.
edits.after: Comeuppance stores bullets from 2500 range — stand behind a minion and it eats them.

edits.before: Use minion dashes to close the distance he wants to keep. His camouflage W only helps if he's out of your Q range. Punish his short auto-attack windows aggressively. Winning trades early denies his scaling comfort.
edits.after: Use minion dashes to close the distance he wants to keep. Wait for Avengerang to be on its 9s cooldown before you step up, then E-stun and burn through the Dirty Fighting shield he gets on every third hit.

edits.before: Punish his cooldowns after W
edits.after: Step up when Avengerang's down

notes: Chart is consistent here — full phases[0..6].side and content win[0..6] both read Irelia, matching the 54.31% win rate, so nothing was moved. Two real fabrications killed: Comeuppance was described as the revive ultimate (the revive is Going Rogue, W) in both whys[4] and spikes[1], and spikes[0] invented an 'auto-crit W'. report[8]'s anti-heal advice was wrong too — Dirty Fighting shields, it does not heal. Left content 'mid' alone: it claims 'group him down before his crit items complete', which I could not source from the kits — flagging rather than guessing at his build path.
